messages:
bryan_sales: Hey team, running a POC demo with MediCore in ap-southeast-1. They started a scripted ramp and we observed a burst of 5xxs (503/502) on their POC route. Can someone triage urgently, customer on call.

lina_se: Thanks. Which model and key are they using? Any request ids?

bryan_sales: They used a hosted trial key, route pinned to rdx-xlarge-v1. Sample header: X-Req-Id: mc-4f9e. Errors: "503 Service Unavailable (Throttle)" and occasionally "502 Bad Gateway".

ops_oncall: I see infra alerts for queue saturation + autoscaler retries. Looks like provider API rate-limited our launch calls. I'll pull logs.

autoscale-bot: alert: autoscale.delay > 30s; queued_requests=900; active_nodes=3; desired_nodes=7.

scott_infra: pasted runtime excerpt for req=mc-4f9e:

```
2026-03-22T02:41:12Z [router] WARN backlog: queue_len=920
2026-03-22T02:41:13Z [autoscaler] INFO decide desired=7 current=3
2026-03-22T02:41:13Z [autoscaler] ERROR provider-api: 429 Too Many Requests on launch
2026-03-22T02:41:14Z [autoscaler] WARN exponential_backoff: retrying launches (attempt=4)
2026-03-22T02:41:15Z [router] ERROR serve: returned 502 to client req=mc-4f9e
```

ops_oncall: Provider 429s caused launch retries to back up; our retry loop exhausted short window and router started returning 5xx. Two-pronged short fix: 1) route this demo to a quantized fallback `rdx-medium-qv1` on the route config; 2) allocate two warm burst nodes in the demo burstpool.

lina_se: I can flip fallback, but need approval to touch burstpool. @scott_infra can you allocate?

scott_infra: allocating burst: `opsctl burst allocate --pool medi-core-demo --count 2`
deploy-bot: job: burst-alloc-1023 accepted.

ops_oncall: also recommending throttling the customer load generator to step down to 250 qps until burst nodes register. Bryan, can you ask them to pause ramp?

bryan_sales: asked them to slow to 200 qps. They agreed. Testing now.

bryan_sales: quick update: error rate dropped to <2% after ~30s. Latency median ~140ms. Customer says demo can continue. :thumbsup:

tara_billing: quick question from customer: will the extra burst nodes or fallback model affect pricing for the trial?

lina_se: fallback reduces compute cost but burstpool uses reserved capacity pricing. For this single short demo we can waive any overage. I'll log a temporary credit request.

scott_infra: root cause: provider-side rate limits + our aggressive immediate retry policy. Action items: 1) add jitter+cap to autoscaler retries; 2) implement demo prewarm option for sales (small warm pool allocation with notice); 3) telemetry: add provider-rate-limit counter to infra dashboard. Filed INF-2041.

ops_oncall: also adding a short term runbook for Sales-run demos: pre-declare expected qps, use prewarm 15m before demo, or enable fallback model on route as safety.

bryan_sales: will update MediCore and schedule a prewarm for their production POC next week.

lina_se: I'll create the billing credit ticket and follow up on comms.

scott_infra: PR incoming to implement backoff change (link will be posted in INF-2041).

bryan_sales: customer-facing blurb for security/comms packet (feel free to copy): "During your demo we briefly returned 5xx responses because our autoscaler was delayed while requesting additional nodes from the cloud provider. We routed your traffic to a lighter-weight model and temporarily allocated extra burst nodes to restore service. Engineering has a ticket to harden the autoscaler retry logic and we will prewarm capacity for your next demo."

ops_oncall: closing for now, will reopen if we see recurrence.
